tracking.name: Global Offshore Wind Alliance (GOWA)
tracking.description: The Global Offshore Wind Alliance (GOWA) is a diplomatic-led multi stakeholder alliance working towards achieving an ambitious uptake of offshore wind through, knowledge sharing, capacity building and strengthening regional collaboration.
tracking.findings: GOWA has strengthened its policy engagement through targeted briefings to members on the fossil fuel crisis, ahead of COP 30, and on floating offshore wind, alongside official submissions to the COP 30 Presidency on the TAFF, to the COP 31 Presidency on barriers and finance for offshore wind, and to the Standing Committee on Finance on ocean finance.

tracking.name: Global Offshore Wind Alliance (GOWA)
tracking.description: The Global Offshore Wind Alliance (GOWA) is a diplomatic-led multi stakeholder alliance working towards achieving an ambitious uptake of offshore wind through, knowledge sharing, capacity building and strengthening regional collaboration.
tracking.findings: GOWA has seen strong growth in its membership, including the welcome addition of its first African government member, as well as a new development bank and civil society organization, further expanding the Alliance’s global reach and strengthening its representation across continents and key stakeholder groups.

tracking.name: Industrial Transition Accelerator (ITA)
tracking.description: The ITA aims to accelerate the number of clean industrial projects reaching final investment decision (FID) across the energy-intensive sectors to build a critical mass of clean industrial plants reaching FID by 2030.
tracking.indicator: Accelerate the pace at which clean industrial projects are financed and built, year-on-year
tracking.findings: 19 Final Investment Decisions (FIDs) were recorded between November 2025 and April 2026, meaning that 2026 is set to be a record year for clean industry investments (a final progress value is to be published on 4 November 2026).

tracking.name: Memorandum of Understanding on Zero-Emission Medium- and Heavy-Duty Vehicles
tracking.description: Countries committing to working together to enable 100% zero-emission new truck and bus sales by 2040.
tracking.indicator: 100% Zero-Emission Medium- and Heavy-Duty Vehicles (Ze-MHDV) sales by 2040
tracking.findings: Together, Global MOU countries have thus far achieved approximately 5% ZE-MHDV sales annually. This figure has increased each year for the past decade and more than doubled between 2024 to 2025.

cases.title: Solutions Bank
cases.initiative: by the Global Offshore Wind Alliance (GOWA)
cases.target: Related CCI target: Policy inputs and briefings
cases.contribution: This action is reported as contributing to Objective 1. Tripling renewables and doubling energy efficiency.
body: As part of its contribution to the Global Climate Action Agenda, GOWA developed and published an openly accessible Solutions Bank, bringing together examples and case studies of best-practice innovation in offshore wind from around the world. The Solutions Bank demonstrates how common challenges to offshore wind development have been overcome and benefits realized, including in relation to energy security, job creation, climate action, nature-positive development and clean energy exports.

By translating experience from offshore wind markets into accessible and replicable lessons, the Solutions Bank strengthens knowledge-sharing and supports countries in moving from ambition towards implementation. In particular, it can help emerging markets identify practical approaches to overcoming barriers, avoid reinventing solutions to common challenges, and accelerate the development of offshore wind in support of shared climate, energy and sustainable development goals.

The Solutions Bank makes practical experience and replicable best practices from offshore wind development freely accessible to governments, policymakers and other stakeholders globally, providing concrete examples of solutions that can be adapted to different national and market contexts. Through its contribution to GCAA, it also strengthens the visibility of offshore wind as a proven and scalable solution for delivering the global energy transition.

cases.title: Mobilizing efforts to accelerate the number of clean industry projects reaching FID year-on-year
cases.target: Related CCI target: Accelerate the pace at which clean industrial projects are financed and built, year-on-year
cases.contribution: This action is reported as contributing to Objective 2. Accelerating zero and low emission technologies in hard-to-abate sectors, and Objective 20. Climate, sustainable and adaptation finance, mainstreaming climate in investments and insurance (under Axis 6).
body: At the local level, the ITA and its partners run country programmes focused on one outcome: final investment decisions (FIDs) on commercial-scale, deep decarbonization projects in energy-intensive sectors. ITA partners with local government, industry and finance players to address the binding constraints that hold projects back, from offtake and power access to infrastructure and financing. At the global level, it works to turn lessons from individual projects into system-level change.

Country work points to six acceleration levers: dependable demand; abundant renewable power; coordinated supply chains; clean trade flows; community support; and catalytic capital. These are taken to decision-makers on the global stage through Build Clean Now - a global collaborative campaign developed by ITA, Mission Possible Partnership and a wide ecosystem of partners that seeks to accelerate the number of clean industry projects reaching FID every year with an initial target of 50 FIDs in 2025-2026.

Globally, clean industrial investment is accelerating: 19 FIDs were recorded between November 2025 and April 2026, as the strategic case for clean industry is getting stronger: clean fuels, chemicals and materials reduce exposure to fossil fuel price shocks and supply disruption. The ITA has supported more than 35 projects in critical sunbelt economies representing USD 80 billion of investment potential.

On global acceleration, Build Clean Now has convened governments, industry and finance through country workshops in Australia, India, Canada, Mexico, Spain; identified and published six acceleration levers (markets, energy, supply chains, trade, communities and finance) drawn from work with project developers worldwide and showcased “Bright Spot” projects to share learnings from operational projects and enable successful approaches to be adopted by others.

cases.title: Expanding network of the Global MOU
cases.initiative: by the Memorandum of Understanding on Zero-Emission Medium- and Heavy-Duty Vehicles
cases.target: Related CCI target: 100% ZE-MHDV Sales by 2040
cases.contribution: This action is reported as contributing to Objective 2. Accelerating zero and low emission technologies in hard-to-abate sectors.
body: Over the past year, the Global MOU has expanded its reach by recruiting new national government signatories alongside subnational and private sector partners, raising ambition for zero-emission medium- and heavy-duty vehicles and accelerating implementation.

The additions of Mexico and Brazil have facilitated connections with key ministries responsible for driving policy forward in two target geographies identified as high priority. Recognizing policy and the implementation of a robust ecosystem of supporting measures to enable the 2030 and 2040 targets of the Global MOU, these connections have been crucial to advocating for the right policy path to ensure fulfillment of these goals. Since the signing, both Brazil and Mexico have been actively engaged in advancing policy and identifying the right windows of opportunity for action. Meetings were held with agencies from the governments and lessons learned from other geographies were brought as part of knowledge exchange.

Over the past year, Mexico, Togo, and Brazil joined the Global MOU, bringing the total number of signatory nations to 43. Alongside this growth in the government network, more than 50 new endorsers from NGOs, the private sector, and subnational governments have signed on.
